clue.text: Count maybe no longer in circulation

definitions.meaning: a count is one example of a titled aristocrat, a peer
an old English gold coin, worth a third of a pound, long since withdrawn

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a count has stopped moving in society.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a nobleman, and the noble was a medieval English gold coin that has not been minted for centuries.

clue.text: Very little drops from this

parts.note: a device that turns liquid medicine into a fine mist of tiny droplets for breathing in

explanation.surface: Hardly anything falls from this.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'very little drops' as tiny droplets, not as almost nothing falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebuliser converts a drug solution into a fine spray inhaled by asthma patients.

clue.text: Feel dispirited and inferior

definitions.meaning: to feel down or depressed, split as two words

explanation.surface: Feeling down and second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means to be in low spirits; as one word it means lower down or lesser.

clue.text: "Speech is of Time, Silence is of " (Carlyle)

definitions.text: "Speech is of Time, Silence is of

parts.words: "Speech is of Time, Silence is of
parts.note: the missing last word of Thomas Carlyle's saying, set against Time: endless duration

explanation.surface: A quotation from Thomas Carlyle with its final word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlyle's line, in Sartor Resartus, contrasts passing time with time without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence is linked with the timeless, the opposite of passing time, which is endlessness.

clue.text: Cases involving incessant letters

indicators.note: involving in its old sense of tangling up, so the letters of the next word are twisted round

explanation.surface: Legal cases built on a ceaseless stream of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' tells you to work with the letters of 'incessant', which 'involving' tangles into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Instances and cases are synonyms: individual examples or occurrences.

clue.text: One in the eye for a girl!

definitions.meaning: the coloured ring around the pupil
a girl's first name, also a flower

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a snub delivered to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is part of the eye, and Iris is a woman's name.

clue.text: When the ratings change it's devastating

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the ratings are to be reordered

explanation.surface: A TV producer finds falling audience figures crushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges THE RATINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattering news is crushing or overwhelming, so devastating.

clue.text: Seaman posted missing

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
something posted has been sent

explanation.surface: A sailor has been listed as missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, gone or missing.

clue.text: The lady never scored highly

parts.note: a female singer whose part is always written in a low register in the score

explanation.surface: A woman who never achieved high marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' suggests marks in an exam; it means written into a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: The contralto is the lowest female singing voice, so her music is never written high.

clue.text: In a bad way, having been given the pip?

definitions.meaning: full of pips, as a fruit is full of seeds

explanation.surface: Feeling poorly after being annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the pip' is British slang for being irritated; here it means supplied with seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means run-down or sickly, and literally means full of seeds.

clue.text: A dancer in an Irish night-club all Erin admires

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A dancer working in a Dublin club whom every Irish patron adores.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'club', all of 'all' and 'Erin', and the start of 'admires'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: Understanding directions given by oriental coppers

parts.note: the sen is a small Japanese coin, historically made of copper
S and E, south and east, compass points

explanation.surface: Grasping the instructions issued by policemen from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests policemen, but here they are low-value coins: the sen of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense, as in making sense of something, means comprehension or grasp.

clue.text: Left unsettled, so making a beastly noise

parts.note: a debt not yet settled is still owing

explanation.surface: Someone left in a disturbed state, and so groaning like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' looks like an anagram signal, but it means an unpaid bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle low, and lowing is the deep moo they make.

clue.text: A swimmer being mean about a painter

indicators.note: about means the miserly word goes around the artist's letters

parts.note: mean in the sense of miserly is stingy
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword stock painter

explanation.surface: A swimmer is being stingy towards an artist friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RA inside STINGY, splitting it STING-RA-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The stingray is a flat fish that swims along the sea floor.

clue.text: The poor will get back tax

parts.note: to back a motion is to second it
rates were a British local property tax

explanation.surface: The needy will have taxes refunded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like 'returned', but it means support, as in seconding a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate means inferior in quality, mediocre.

clue.text: Take water with these cocktails, dear

indicators.note: cocktails are mixed drinks, so these words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to dilute some mixed drinks, addressed to a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktails' mixes the letters of WATER and THESE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear and sweetheart are both terms of endearment for a beloved.

clue.text: Use no offensive language

parts.note: to swap a blunt or unpleasant term for a gentler, milder one

explanation.surface: An instruction not to swear.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism is a mild word substituted for a harsh one, so to speak in euphemisms avoids giving offence.

clue.text: An island's effective come-back

indicators.note: a come-back returns the way it came, so the word for effective is read backwards

parts.note: able, as in an able performer, means competent or effective

explanation.surface: An island is staging an impressive revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come-back' turns ABLE round. Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was first exiled; his own come-back from it fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is an Italian island off Tuscany.

clue.text: Women players receiving part-payment

parts.note: female performers who are paid for taking a role, a part

explanation.surface: Sportswomen getting an instalment of their wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part-payment' looks like an instalment; it is payment for playing a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Actresses are women who perform roles on stage or screen.

clue.text: Left temporary settlement in deed!

indicators.note: in means the settlement goes inside the word deed

parts.note: a camp is a temporary settlement of tents or huts

explanation.surface: Departed from a makeshift encampment, and did so indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CAMP inside DEED, splitting it DE-CAMP-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, so decamped means went away.

clue.text: Small animal keeping little page totally absorbed

indicators.note: keeping means the creature holds the page letter within it

parts.note: a rat is a small rodent
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A small pet holds a tiny book page, completely engrossed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts P inside RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rapt is enthralled, wholly engrossed in something.

clue.text: Declared the loser in ten seconds flat

definitions.text: Declared the loser in ten seconds flat

parts.words: Declared the loser in ten seconds flat
parts.note: a boxer knocked down and still on the canvas while the referee reaches ten loses the bout; 'flat' is the floored fighter

explanation.surface: Someone was beaten remarkably quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten seconds flat' reads as a fast time, but it is the referee's ten-second count over a fighter lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing, a fighter still down when the referee has called ten is ruled to have lost.

clue.text: Main way to get round a regulation in the country

indicators.note: to get round means the road surrounds the other letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, London to Leeds, written MI
a law is a regulation

explanation.surface: A motorway diverted around some bylaw in a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get round' suggests evading a rule; here M1 literally encircles A LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked country in south-east Africa.

clue.text: They'll wait, all at sea

parts.note: waiting here means serving at table, done by attendants on a ship, not hanging about confused

explanation.surface: People who will hang about, utterly bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' suggests confusion, but it means literally on board ship, where cabin staff wait on passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are the attendants who serve passengers on a ship or plane.

clue.text: The first of several given a pound by Evelyn Waugh

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, like a coop

explanation.surface: Waugh hands over a pound note to the first of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money, but it is a pen; Scoop is Evelyn Waugh's 1938 satire on journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoop is a novel written by the English author Evelyn Waugh.

clue.text: Model socialist leader getting together with liberal

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a liberal helping is a generous or ample one

explanation.surface: An exemplary left-wing leader forms a coalition with a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' looks political, but it means plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a specimen or example, a model of the whole.

clue.text: Quietly employ about fifty beat that!

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: about means the word for employ goes around the numeral

parts.note: to employ is to use
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A challenge: use a quiet approach for around fifty, and top that!
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside USE to give ULSE after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a rhythmic beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Such a gait is only right in a small child

indicators.note: in means the letter for right goes inside the child

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A small child can only manage a certain way of walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a gait between walking and running, as of a horse.

clue.text: Special board arranging Franco- German agreement

parts.note: the French word for yes, as the first half of the agreement
the German word for yes, as the second half

explanation.surface: A board specially set up to arrange a treaty between France and Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The agreement is two people each saying yes in their own language, French then German.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a lettered board used at seances to receive supposed messages from spirits.

clue.text: Citadel taking a cut and turning over store

parts.note: to crop is to cut short

indicators.note: turning over means the word for a store is reversed

parts.note: a silo is a store for grain

explanation.surface: A fortress taking reductions and having its stores turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses SILO to give OLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified upper part of an ancient Greek city, a citadel.

clue.text: A top man pretends to be upset about one

indicators.note: about means the jumbled word goes around the numeral
upset means the letters of pretends are overturned and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A leading figure is putting on a show of being distressed about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be upset' rearranges PRETENDS, and 'about' places I inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a republic or organisation.

clue.text: Prepare the medical attendant with a letter

parts.note: DR is short for doctor
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: Getting the doctor ready, along with a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Dress here means prepare, as in dressing a salad or a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress food or timber is to make it ready for use.
